answer: Temporal Accumulation Gate. A new identity's request rate starts throttled and only widens after a sustained history of well-paced traffic, so a bot farm cannot forge the slow ramp without paying real wall-clock time per account. Each identity must also hold an aging token whose age advances only during idle gaps, meaning attackers cannot batch-create agents to appear old—costing them days of calendar delay and idle capacity per identity. The ledger brands each token with a rotating onyx marker to prevent pre-aging and resale, and any fast burst trips a reset to the ivory baseline tier.
